Subject: SDK Lab: environment handoff & routing/auth checklist

Hi Samantha — great to meet today, thanks for the time. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned before the lab kickoff.

Summary of what we agreed
- Goal: run a two-hour hands-on SDK lab (Python + TypeScript) to validate integration patterns: auth, routing, structured output / tool-calling, embeddings + reranking.
- Success criteria: local sample apps run end-to-end, authenticated calls to a Redwood staging endpoint, a small semantic search using embeddings, and a reranker run against sample candidate outputs.

Immediate action items (who/when)
1) Redwood: share lab plan + sample repo (I attached the plan and a repo link) — target: tomorrow EOD PST (Karthik).
2) Ava Systems: confirm 2 engineers for the lab and whether they’ll use macOS/Linux/Windows WSL (Samantha) — please reply with names by EOD tomorrow.
3) Both: agree on routing & cost policy for the lab (we recommend US-west for lower latency/cost and fall back to us-east) — we’ll validate during runbook.

Technical notes / quick checklist (things to prep locally)
- Auth: use an API key with scopes: read:models, infer:run, embeddings:write. See attached redwood-auth-scope-matrix.csv for the exact scope names.
- Env vars (example): REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_REGION (us-west/us-east), REDWOOD_MODEL (text-generation or embed), REDWOOD_RERANK_MODEL.
- Local testing: the sample apps run on CPU for small prompts; GPU is optional for performance testing. We’ll include a Docker Compose so you can run identical containers.
- Routing: sample config supports static region pinning and cost-priority rules (we’ll walk through a simple routing policy file).
- Structured output/tool calling: we’ll demo a TypeScript sample that uses function-calling style responses and a Python example that maps structured JSON to an internal tool invocation.
- Embeddings/rerankers: we’ll produce embeddings for a ~500-row doc set (small) and demonstrate a two-stage retrieval + rerank pattern.

Files attached: redwood-sdk-lab-plan.pdf, sample-apps-repo-link.txt (contains GitHub URL), env-example.env.

Next step: please confirm the engineer names and preferred OS and whether you want the lab to be split into two 1-hour sessions or a single 2-hour block. I’ll schedule/confirm once you reply.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

— Karthik

On Mon, Jun 21, 2026 at 4:02 PM Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Samantha — great to meet today, thanks for the time. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned before the lab kickoff.

Thanks for the fast reply and the attendee list — great to have Brandon and Priya. Answers below and a few runnable commands to sanity-check locally before the lab.

1) CPU vs GPU: Yes, the Python sample apps can run entirely on CPU for functional validation. Performance will be lower (inference times per request), but the control flow, function-calls, embeddings, and reranking all work the same. For local dev please set REDWOOD_RUNTIME=PytorchCPU in env-example.env.

2) Embedding memory footprint: for a 500-row dataset using the default embed model (redwood-embed-1-small) you should expect ~100-200 MB of RAM for in-memory vectors (float32). If you use float16 quantization or store on-disk (faiss index with mmap) it can drop under 50MB. We’ll show both options during the lab.

3) Network pre-flight: ensure outbound HTTPS (443) to api.redwood.com and our staging host api-staging.redwood.com is allowed; IP ranges will be provided if you need firewall rules. Also allow WebSocket (wss) if you plan to use streaming responses from the TS sample.

Quick local sanity commands (from repo root):
- clone: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-sample-apps.git
- python env: python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
- install: pip install -r python/requirements.txt
- run: REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-demo REDWOOD_REGION=us-west python python/sample_app.py --mode=smoke

TypeScript quickstart (node 16+):
- cd typescript && npm ci
- export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-demo && export REDWOOD_REGION=us-west
- npm run dev (dev server includes a web UI that demonstrates function-calling and structured output)

Function-calling / structured output notes:
- The TS sample uses a function schema to request a structured JSON reply that we map to a mocked tool. We validate the JSON schema locally with ajv before invoking.
- The Python sample shows an example of receiving a 'tool_call' object in the response and then executing a local HTTP call to a mocked internal API.

Embeddings + rerank pattern:
- Stage 1: embed candidates with redwood-embed-1-small, index with FAISS (demo script included).
- Stage 2: retrieve top-50, then hit redwood-rerank-1 to reorder by relevance using the reranker scoring API. We’ll include sample payloads in the repo.

Attachments I’ve uploaded to the Drive folder and attached the lab plan here: redwood-sdk-lab-plan.pdf. Also included env-example.env and the scope matrix.

Slots: Tue 10:00–11:00 PT and Wed 10:00–11:00 PT both work for our team — I’ll send calendar invites once you confirm.

Retention: by default Redwood demo logs are retained for 30 days in staging; we can reduce to 7 days for the lab if you prefer. No customer data will be persisted beyond the agreed retention and everything in the lab will be marked as demo/test. If you need an audit export we can provide a CSV extract.

If that all sounds good, please confirm and I’ll book invites.

— Karthik
